主要内容: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) released data on Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by industry for the second quarter of 2019, showing a 2.0 percent increase in real GDP. Professional, scientific, and technical services, real estate and rental and leasing, and mining were the leading contributors to the growth. The professional, scientific, and technical services industry saw a 7.4 percent increase in real value added, while real estate and rental and leasing increased by 2.6 percent. Mining experienced a 23.5 percent rise, primarily due to oil and gas extraction. However, the growth slowed compared to the first quarter, with finance and insurance being the main contributor to the deceleration. Retail trade also saw a slowdown, contributing to the overall decrease in growth. The data highlights the performance of various industry groups and their impact on the U.S. economy. The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) released data showing that the second quarter of 2019 saw a 2.7 percent increase in GDP, following a 2.8 percent rise in the first quarter. The growth was primarily driven by the retail sector, particularly nonstore retailers. Real estate and rental and leasing also saw a 3.9 percent increase, while professional, scientific, and technical services grew by 6.5 percent, largely due to an uptick in advertising, research and development, and engineering services. The report reflects the annual update of the Industry Economic Accounts, covering the first quarter of 2014 through the first quarter of 2019. Key improvements include updated data on video streaming revenue and revised source data from the Census Bureau, Bureau of Labor Statistics, and Department of Treasury. The report highlights the importance of quality-adjusted pricing for cellular phones and enhanced coverage for streaming providers. The next release is scheduled for January 9, 2020, for the third quarter of 2019.

涉及行业.名称: Real estate and rental and leasing
